body.en: Early one morning Mourad wakes Aram and shows him a beautiful white *horse*. Aram longs to ride and is torn between joy and his knowledge that the horse must have been stolen. The boys ride together through the countryside in the early light.

say.en: Mourad wakes Aram very early in the morning.
Outside stands a beautiful white horse.
Aram wonders whether this is stealing, and argues himself out of it.
The boys ride together through the countryside.
Aram rides alone, is thrown, and the horse runs off.
Mourad recovers it, and they hide it in an old vineyard barn.

problem.en: How does Aram convince himself that riding the horse is not stealing?

steps.en: Aram knows the family is too poor to buy a horse.
He also knows the family is proud of its honesty.
He decides it is not stealing as long as they do not sell the horse.

answer.en: Aram knows his poor family could never buy such a horse, yet they are famously honest. He resolves the conflict with childish logic: it would only be stealing if they offered the horse for sale, so riding it is not a crime.
